ipfs_assessment: IPFS is a reasonable fit for immutable, content-addressed Seed Package storage, and it gives you tamper-evidence via CID. However, kubo is heavyweight for light peer nodes, and public DHT discovery can be slow and flaky. For a more controlled exchange, wrapping IPFS with a libp2p-based gossip layer or using a dedicated DHT (e.g., js-libp2p or a private IPFS swarm) would improve discovery and latency. Content addressing alone is not enough for a trust model — you must sign package manifests (ECDSA/Ed25519) to bind each tag set to a peer identity, and include explicit provenance metadata internally.
scaling_to_thousands: IPFS/kubo can technically scale to thousands of nodes, but the public DHT and provider-record lookups become a bottleneck: publish latency and lookup failure rates rise, and each node's resource consumption (connections, memory, disk) grows superlinearly if not tuned. For 1,000+ nodes, you should run a private libp2p network with dedicated bootstrap peers and optional delegated routing. For 10,000+, move to a more structured overlay for metadata discovery (e.g., gossipsub for announcements) while using IPFS only for blob storage. Also use content-addressed package metadata that can be replicated through a smaller of set of active relays.
tag_bandwidth_sufficient: Sharing only structured tags is sufficient only if the tag schema is expressive enough to carry the relevant semantic content — e.g., raw judgment text, confidence scores, dimension labels, context anchors, and relationship edges. If tags are just sparse tokens, knowledge exchange will be too lossy to be useful. On the technical side, text tags are cheap to replicate, so bandwidth is not the real constraint — semantic integrity and annotation quality are. You should add versioned tag vocabularies and embeddings so nodes can align meaning across different sources.
convergence_in_p2p: Without a central aggregator, convergence measurement must be done with a distributed averaging / opinion dynamics protocol. Each node maintains a local model of the aggregate tag distribution, gossips summary statistics, and applies bounded updates (e.g., push-sum or push-pull gossip). Use overlapping tags as a similarity metric and calculate distance to a locally observed 'consensus' estimate. This can be made robust with cryptographic accumulation (Merkle roots of tag sets) and periodic comparison against sampled peers.
spam_poisoning_defense: There is a real risk of malicious nodes publishing bad tags. Defend with: (1) signed identities and a Web-of-Trust/reputation score; (2) publish gates — a peer must build reputation before its tags are propagated widely; (3) tag validation rules (schema, required fields, provenance linkage); (4) content-level scoring via cross-peer agreement checks — a tag that contradicts the consensus of multiple known peers gets lower weight; (5) optional Proof-of-Work for package publication to slow sybil attacks; and (6) redundant random sampling from the DHT before accepting foreign tags.
weakest_part: The weakest part is the lack of authenticated, tamper-evident provenance and update semantics. CIDs only prove a byte-identical package, but they do not tell who published the package, when, nor whether it supersedes an earlier one. The current design has no signed manifests, no peer identity binding, and no conflict resolution for tag updates, so a malicious node can republish a valid CID from another node without accountability, or publish conflicting packages under the same logical source. Also, 'resolve' based purely on IPFS directory walking is fragile and gives no semantic integrity checks.
should_evolve_to: Keep IPFS for content storage, but evolve the exchange layer to a hybrid: use libp2p pubsub (gossipsub) for package announcements and resolved-tag streams; sign and timestamp package manifests; and use delta/CRDT state for mutable tag indexes. This gives you real-time propagation, provenance, and convergence tracking while retaining content-addressing for the immutable payloads. If full decentralization remains critical, consider dsnp or similar but libp2p + CRDT is the most pragmatic progression.
verdict: P2P exchange is the right keystone for this project, but you must strengthen it with signed identities, trust-based propagation, and a gossip/CRDT synchronization layer before it can serve as the trust backbone of a large-scale network.
